handed asymmetry in bilateral animals requires three components: (i) a mechanism to generate molecular handedness, which we call conversion; (ii) a process to generate random handed asymmetry, which can be biased by the handedness generated by the conversion process; and (iii) a tissue specific mechanism for interpreting handedness.
